navire.note: A more formal word than bateau.

batiment.note: In this chapter it is nautical, not a building.

armateur.note: A person or company that equips and operates merchant ships.

curieux.note: As a noun here, people who gather to watch.

mouillage.note: The act or place of anchoring a ship.

beaupre.note: A spar projecting from the front of a sailing ship.

huniers.note: Sails set above the lower sails.

foc.note: A triangular sail near the front of a ship.

brigantine.note: A fore-and-aft sail on the after mast.

allure.note: Here it describes the ship's slow, sad entrance.

bord.note: A bord means aboard a ship.

barque.note: A small craft used in the harbor.

muraille.note: Here, the side of the ship.

chargement.note: The goods carried by the ship.

cargaison.note: The load of goods on a vessel.

fievre-cerebrale.note: An older expression for a severe fever affecting the brain.

cargues.note: Ropes used to gather in sails.

hamac.note: Used here in the burial at sea description.

boulet.note: Used as a weight in the burial at sea.

escompter.note: Here, to count a voyage's profit in advance.

douane.note: Officials who inspect goods entering port.
